references.text: Moses gave the same command not to leave the entrance of the tent of meeting during the consecration period, showing that the anointing oil required the priests to remain in the holy place.
The high priest was not to leave the sanctuary or profane it, because the anointing oil of his God was upon him—the same principle found in Leviticus 10:7.
Anointing with the holy oil as part of priestly consecration establishes the basis for why Aaron and his sons could not leave the tent.
Moses poured the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to consecrate him, explaining the expression 'the Lord's anointing oil is upon you.'
Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they offered unauthorized fire—the context for why the remaining priests had to obey strictly.
Ezekiel describes how priests were not to go out into the outer court without changing their garments, to preserve holiness—a similar principle regarding priestly movements in the sanctuary.
